questions.title: Section A – Multiple Choice, Terms, Matching & Diagrams

subQuestions.questionText:
The part in the amniotic egg that provides nutrients to the developing embryo:

A Yolk
B Chorion
C Amnion
D Shell

Which gland is responsible for the secretion of prolactin?

A Thyroid gland
B Adrenal gland
C Ovary
D Pituitary gland

After an accident, a person can still walk, but has poor control and coordination of the skeletal muscles. Which parts of the central nervous system (K = cerebrum, L = cerebellum, M = spinal cord) are probably damaged?

A K, L and M
B K and L
C K and M
D L and M

The cranial and spinal nerves are part of the … nervous system.

A central
B peripheral
C sympathetic
D parasympathetic

The following changes occur at puberty: (i) Growth of facial hair, (ii) Deepening of the voice, (iii) Onset of menstruation, (iv) Oily skin. Which combination of characteristics occurs due to the secretion of testosterone?

A (i), (ii) and (iii) only
B (ii) and (iii) only
C (i), (ii) and (iv) only
D (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)

A man is fertile if his semen contains a minimum of 20 million sperm per cm³ and at least 75% of the sperm cells are active. Identify the sample obtained from an infertile man:

A 23 million/cm³, 30% inactive
B 25 million/cm³, 20% inactive
C 22 million/cm³, 25% inactive
D 20 million/cm³, 15% inactive

Which ONE of the following is a cause of short-sightedness?

A The eyeball is too short.
B The lens is unable to become less convex.
C The lens is opaque.
D The surface of the eye is uneven.

options.B: The lens is unable to become less convex.
options.D: The surface of the eye is uneven.

subQuestions.questionText:
A person has a disorder where she is unable to secrete ADH. It is most likely that …

A the renal tubules will become more permeable to water.
B the blood will have a higher volume of water.
C large volumes of urine will be produced.
D more water is reabsorbed by the renal tubules.

options.A: the renal tubules will become more permeable to water.
options.B: the blood will have a higher volume of water.
options.C: large volumes of urine will be produced.
options.D: more water is reabsorbed by the renal tubules.

subQuestions.questionText:
Eagles are birds that lay their eggs high up on mountain cliffs and feed their young once they hatch. Which combination of reproductive strategies applies to eagles? (i) Internal fertilisation, (ii) External fertilisation, (iii) Precocial development, (iv) Parental care, (v) Ovipary

A (i), (ii) and (iii) only
B (i), (iv) and (v) only
C (ii) and (iii) only
D (ii), (iii) and (iv) only

The flow diagram represents a part of the homeostasis of compound X: [Increase in concentration of X in blood → Receptor cells in Y are stimulated → Impulses are sent to Z]. Which ONE of the following combinations is CORRECT?

A X=Carbon dioxide, Y=Hypothalamus, Z=Pituitary gland
B X=Water, Y=Hypothalamus, Z=Medulla oblongata
C X=Carbon dioxide, Y=Carotid artery, Z=Medulla oblongata
D X=Water, Y=Carotid artery, Z=Pituitary gland

options.C: X=Carbon dioxide, Y=Carotid artery, Z=Medulla oblongata

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for: The inner lining of the uterus.
Give the correct biological term for: A brain disorder that results in confusion and memory loss.
Give the correct biological term for: The plant hormone that plays a role in the falling of leaves from trees.
Give the correct biological term for: A reproductive strategy where the foetus develops inside the uterus.
Give the correct biological term for: The type of vision in which both eyes are used to see one image.
Give the correct biological term for: The part of the brain that joins the left and the right hemispheres of the cerebrum.
Give the correct biological term for: The membrane in the amniotic egg that collects nitrogenous waste.
Give the correct biological term for: The plant hormone used to control the growth of weeds.

Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B, or NONE.

Description: A larger number of male and female gametes are produced.
A: External fertilisation
B: Internal fertilisation

Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B, or NONE.

Description: A plant defence mechanism.
A: Thorns
B: Chemicals

Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B, or NONE.

Description: Contributes to the movement of sperm.
A: Mitochondria
B: Tail

The diagram represents a part of the menstrual cycle that occurs in the human ovary (showing follicle development, ovulation, and corpus luteum). Name the part of the menstrual cycle represented by the diagram.

subQuestions.label: 1.4.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify structure A in the ovarian cycle diagram.

subQuestions.label: 1.4.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify structure B in the ovarian cycle diagram.

subQuestions.label: 1.4.2(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify structure C in the ovarian cycle diagram.

subQuestions.label: 1.4.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Name the hormone that controls the development of structure A (Graafian follicle).

subQuestions.label: 1.4.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Name the hormone that is secreted by structure A (Graafian follicle).

subQuestions.label: 1.4.3(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Name the hormone that stimulates the process occurring at structure D (ovulation).

subQuestions.label: 1.5.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: The diagram represents the human eye (parts labelled A–H). Identify part D.

subQuestions.label: 1.5.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify part E in the human eye diagram.

subQuestions.label: 1.5.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Give the LETTER of the Choroid in the human eye diagram.

subQuestions.label: 1.5.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Give the LETTER of the Iris in the human eye diagram.
Name the TWO different receptors found in part A (retina) of the human eye.
Give only the LETTERS of THREE parts in the human eye diagram that are involved in accommodation of the eye.
subQuestions.memoText: B, G, H (any three correct from: B = lens, G = ciliary muscle/suspensory ligament, H = suspensory ligament/ciliary muscle). Mark first THREE only.

questions.title: Human Reproduction, Embryonic Development, Basal Body Temperature, Hearing Loss & Alcohol Investigation

subQuestions.label: 2.1.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: The diagram shows the male reproductive system (parts A–F with Epididymis labelled). Identify part E.

subQuestions.label: 2.1.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify part F in the male reproductive system diagram.

subQuestions.label: 2.1.1(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify part C in the male reproductive system diagram.
Name the type of gametogenesis that occurs in part D (testes/seminiferous tubules).
Describe the process of spermatogenesis.
subQuestions.memoText: Under the influence of testosterone, diploid cells / germinal epithelium in the seminiferous tubules of the testes undergo meiosis to form haploid sperm cells. (Any 4 points)

subQuestions.questionText: Epididymitis causes inflammation in the epididymis, creating a blockage between the testes and part B (vas deferens). Explain how this affects the composition of semen.
subQuestions.memoText: Sperm are prevented from entering the vas deferens / leaving the testes, resulting in few sperm / a low sperm count in the semen.

subQuestions.label: 2.2.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: The diagram represents human embryonic development (Sperm cell + A → B → morula → C → Embryo). Identify Cell B.

subQuestions.label: 2.2.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify Structure C in the embryonic development diagram.
Explain the difference between cell A (ovum) and cell B (zygote) in the embryonic development diagram.
subQuestions.memoText: Cell A is haploid / has 23 chromosomes / contains the genetic material of the female only. Cell B is diploid / has 46 chromosomes / contains the genetic material of both parents. Cell A is not fertilised / Cell B is fertilised.

subQuestions.questionText: Name the fluid surrounding the embryo.
State THREE functions of amniotic fluid.
subQuestions.memoText: Any three of: Allows for free movement of the foetus; Protects the foetus against mechanical injury / acts as a shock absorber; Prevents dehydration of the foetus; Prevents temperature changes. (Mark first THREE only.)

subQuestions.label: 2.3.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Use the graph of body temperature over a 28-day menstrual cycle to identify the basal body temperature for this woman.

subQuestions.label: 2.3.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Use the graph to identify the day of ovulation for this woman.
Using evidence in the graph, give a reason for your identification of the day of ovulation.
subQuestions.memoText: Body temperature increased above basal body temperature / 36.2°C immediately after day 16.

subQuestions.questionText: Progesterone causes an increase in basal body temperature. Explain why the increase in basal body temperature occurs only after ovulation.
subQuestions.memoText: The corpus luteum is formed after ovulation and it secretes progesterone.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why basal body temperature is measured when a person is at rest.
subQuestions.memoText: Physical activity / increased cellular respiration changes body temperature. Low physical activity / cellular respiration prevents a change in body temperature, ensuring the reading reflects the basal level only.

subQuestions.label: 2.4.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: The diagram represents the human ear (parts P, Q, R, S, T). Write down only the LETTERS of TWO parts that may be damaged when a person suffers from Type A hearing loss (blockage in outer and middle ear).
subQuestions.memoText: P and T (Mark first TWO only)

subQuestions.label: 2.4.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Write down only the LETTERS of TWO parts that may be damaged when a person suffers from Type B hearing loss (damage to inner ear receptors or nerves).
subQuestions.memoText: S and R (Mark first TWO only)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify part S in the human ear diagram.
Describe the role of the hearing receptors when they are stimulated by pressure waves.
subQuestions.memoText: They convert the stimulus / pressure waves to an impulse and transfer it to the auditory nerve.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why a person will suffer from hearing loss if the bones at P (ossicles) are fused.
subQuestions.memoText: Ossicles will not vibrate freely / fewer / no vibrations will be carried to the oval window; there is decreased amplification of sound; fewer / no pressure waves will form in the cochlea; receptors in the cochlea will not be stimulated / stimulated less; less / no impulses will reach the cerebrum. (1 compulsory + any 3)

subQuestions.label: 2.5.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Scientists investigated the effect of different doses of alcohol on reaction time in 30-year-old male volunteers over 7 days. State the independent variable for this investigation.

subQuestions.label: 2.5.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: State the dependent variable for the alcohol–reaction time investigation.
Name TWO variables that were controlled during the alcohol–reaction time investigation.
subQuestions.memoText: Any two of: Age (30 years old); Gender (men); Volunteers were tested over a period of 7 days; Volunteers abstained from alcohol for 24 hours prior to testing; Reaction time was measured 30 minutes after consuming the alcohol. (Mark first TWO only.)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO ways in which the reliability of the results can be improved.
subQuestions.memoText: Use more than 2 volunteers / increase the number of volunteers; Repeat the investigation / take multiple readings for the same dose. (Mark first TWO only.)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why the participants only received alcohol every second day.
subQuestions.memoText: To ensure that there is no alcohol in the body and that only the alcohol given on the day is tested for.

subQuestions.questionText: Male 1 has a body mass of 93 kg. Calculate the amount of alcohol (in mg) that he consumed on day 7 of the investigation (dose = 600 mg/kg). Show ALL working.
State a conclusion for the alcohol–reaction time investigation.
subQuestions.memoText: Higher doses of alcohol increase the reaction time.

questions.title: Nervous System, Homeostasis, Thermoregulation, Osmoregulation & Plant Responses

subQuestions.label: 3.1.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: The diagram represents part of a reflex arc (Receptor, Neuron A, Neuron E, Neuron D, Effector, with structures B and C labelled). Give the LETTER of the part that represents the dorsal root.

subQuestions.label: 3.1.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Give the LETTER of the part that represents the sensory neuron.
State the significance of a synapse.
subQuestions.memoText: It ensures that nerve impulses are transmitted in one direction.

subQuestions.label: 3.1.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Explain the significance of a reflex action.
subQuestions.memoText: It is a rapid / automatic reaction to a stimulus that protects the body from damage.

subQuestions.label: 3.1.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Explain the effect on the reflex arc if neuron A (sensory neuron) is cut.
subQuestions.memoText: No impulse will be transmitted from the receptor to the spinal cord / interneuron and the effector will not be stimulated.

subQuestions.questionText: Draw a labelled diagram to show the detailed structure of neuron D (motor neuron).
subQuestions.memoText: Mark scheme (5 marks): Diagram of a motor neuron (D) – 1 mark; Correct caption – 1 mark; Any three correct labels from: nucleus, axon, myelin sheath, cell body, cytoplasm, dendrite – 3 marks.

subQuestions.label: 3.2.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: In the context of insulin pumps and diabetes mellitus: Identify the groups of cells in the pancreas that contain the beta cells.

subQuestions.label: 3.2.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the signal for the insulin pump to turn on and start pumping insulin.
subQuestions.memoText: A high concentration of glucose in the blood

subQuestions.questionText: State why the Islets of Langerhans have endocrine characteristics.
subQuestions.memoText: They secrete hormones / insulin / glucagon directly into the blood / have no ducts.

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the effect of insulin on the liver and the muscles.
subQuestions.memoText: It stimulates the conversion of glucose to glycogen and it promotes the absorption / usage of glucose by the cells.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why electronic insulin pumps are more effective in controlling blood glucose levels than insulin injections.
subQuestions.memoText: It delivers insulin specifically according to the glucose level, to allow for better blood glucose management / regular dosing.

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the role of the human skin in the regulation of body temperature on a cold day.
subQuestions.memoText: Any 6 of: (Cold) receptors in the skin convert the stimulus to an impulse which is sent to the hypothalamus that stimulates vasoconstriction in the skin / stimulates blood vessels of the skin to constrict; less blood flows to the skin / sweat glands; less heat is lost (from the skin) through radiation; the sweat glands are stimulated to produce less sweat and less heat is lost through evaporation of sweat.

subQuestions.label: 3.4.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: The table shows blood salt levels of a group of people: Lower than 136 mmol/ℓ = 5 people; 136–140 = 15; 141–145 = 21; Higher than 145 = 4. Use data to determine how many people have hypernatremia.

subQuestions.label: 3.4.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Use the data to determine how many people have normal blood salt levels.
Describe how the human body increases a salt level lower than 136 mmol/ℓ to the normal level.
subQuestions.memoText: Receptor cells detect the low salt level; the adrenal glands are stimulated and more aldosterone is secreted; in the renal tubules the reabsorption of salt / sodium is increased into the surrounding blood capillaries; less salt is excreted. (Any 6 points)

subQuestions.questionText: Draw a histogram to show the results of the blood salt level data (Lower than 136: 5 people; 136–140: 15; 141–145: 21; Higher than 145: 4).
subQuestions.memoText: Mark scheme (6 marks): Correct type of graph – histogram drawn (1); Caption of graph including both variables (1); Axes correctly labelled with correct unit for x-axis (1); Scale for x- and y-axes – equal width bars with no spaces; correct y-axis scale (1); Plotting 1–3 coordinates correctly (1), all four coordinates correctly (2). Bars at heights: 5, 15, 21, 4.

subQuestions.questionText: An investigation used clinostats and unilateral light to test plant seedling responses (Apparatus A: clinostat on, seedlings grow straight; Apparatus B: clinostat off, seedlings bend toward light). Identify the plant growth response demonstrated by the results.
In which apparatus (A or B) was the clinostat switched on and the disc rotating slowly?
Explain your answer to question 3.5.2 (why Apparatus B had the clinostat switched on).
subQuestions.memoText: All the seedlings in Apparatus B grew straight up / showed no phototropism because they were evenly exposed to light / not exposed to unilateral light / equal distribution of auxins.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the growth response of the seedlings in apparatus A (clinostat off, unilateral light, seedlings bend toward light).
subQuestions.memoText: The seedlings / stems grew / bent to the left / towards light because they were exposed to light from one side / unilateral light; auxins diffuse to the right / dark side of the seedlings; the high concentration of auxins on the right / dark side stimulates cell elongation / cell division / growth on that side.
